quote: The goal is to reframe such arguments to be more trustworthy (e.g., less partisan, no appeal to fear fallacy), while maintaining the same denotative meaning of the input argument. We introduce our approach called ENTRUST : ArgumENT Reframing with langUage modelS and enTailment
We introduce our approach called ENTRUST ... a method for argument reframing ... we fine-tune BART on our parallel data ... to generate reframed arguments.

We introduce our approach called ENTRUST : ArgumENT Reframing with langUage modelS and enTailment, with the following contributions: 1) A Connotation-guided Masked Language Model approach to generate a parallel dataset of naturally occuring arguments and their reframings (Section 2); 2) A method for argument reframing that combines controllable text generation (connotative meaning associated with trust) and entailment (same denotative meaning) (Section 3);
datasets: Appeal to Fear or Prejudice dataset
outputs: Reframed arguments (text) with altered connotation but preserved denotation
reframed arguments with same denotation but improved connotation (e.g., less partisan, reduced fear)

We use Amazon Mechanical Turk to evaluate on a total of 900 utterances ... We proposed a set of 3 criteria to evaluate the generated output: (1) Fluency (F), (2) Meaning Preservation (M), (3) Trustworthiness/Presence of Fear (T/PF).
We use Amazon Mechanical Turk to evaluate on a total of 900 utterances, 750 generated from 5 systems and 150 utterances generated by humans.
guideline: Turkers were asked to rate reframed arguments based on fluency, meaning preservation, trustworthiness (for partisan arguments), and presence of fear (for appeal to fear fallacies)
Human raters were asked to rate each generated argument on Fluency, Meaning Preservation, Trustworthiness (for partisan) or Presence of Fear (for appeal-to-fear).

We proposed a set of 3 criteria to evaluate the generated output: (1) Fluency (F) ("How fluent and grammat-ical are the utterances?"), (2) Meaning Preservation (M) ("How well does the reframed argument capture the same denotative meaning as the input argument?"), (3) Trustworthiness/Presence of Fear(T/PF).
